fix(ci): pin the release build to ubuntu-24.04

## What and why

- **Runner:** Pin the Linux release build to Ubuntu 24.04, matching the workflow’s enforced glibc and WebKitGTK baseline. The failed run received Ubuntu 26.04 via `ubuntu-latest`.

## Verified

- Failure logs confirmed the runner was Ubuntu 26.04; workflow YAML parses successfully.

## Not verified

- The release build has not been rerun.

## Checklist

- [ ] `make check` clean (gofmt, tidy, vet also with `-tags production`, `go test -race`)
- [ ] Docs / README updated
- [ ] No fixtures or demo code reachable from a production build

fix(ci): retry Lighthouse runs that fail with NO_NAVSTART

Lighthouse on main failed with `NO_NAVSTART` (Chrome could not record the trace), a transient error that passed on the next run. Retry each Lighthouse run up to 3 times before failing.

fix: honor signed application version equivalences

Refs petauron/senlun#244

A catalog release can contain a signed, exact equivalence between an installed package and the available package. Check it only against the accepted official TUF target and exact version and recipe revision; missing, stale or invalid metadata keeps the normal update indication. Installed receipts, node identities and application data are not changed. A different available version or recipe revision is never suppressed.

Uses existing TUF and JSON dependencies.

fix(templating)!: remove template functions that expose the operator environment


## Pull Request type

Please check the type of change your PR introduces:

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, renaming)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no API changes)
- [ ] Build-related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] Other (please describe):

## What is the current behavior?

Templates were built with all sprout registries, including env (`env`,
`expandEnv`), which read environment variables of the operator process,
such as ARGOCD_GENERATOR_TOKEN. Template output ends up in labels and
ArgoCD parameters that tenants can read. The backward registry also
provided `getHostByName`, which performs DNS lookups from the operator,
also during admission.

## What is the new behavior?

Replace all.RegistryGroup() with an explicit list of registries without
env, and remove getHostByName. The filesystem and network registries stay:
they only manipulate path strings and parse IPs/CIDRs.

Documents the unavailable functions and that templates should only use
values that may be shared with tenants.

## Does this introduce a breaking change?

- [x] Yes
- [ ] No

## Other information

BREAKING CHANGE: templates using env, expandEnv or getHostByName fail.

+package argocd_plugin_generator
+
+import (
+	"bytes"
+	"sync"
+
+	"github.com/belastingdienst/opr-paas/v5/internal/logging"
+	. "github.com/onsi/ginkgo/v2"
+	"github.com/rs/zerolog"
+	"github.com/rs/zerolog/log"
+)
+
+// syncBuffer is a bytes.Buffer that is safe for concurrent use (e.g. by an httptest server goroutine).
+type syncBuffer struct {
+	mu  sync.Mutex
+	buf bytes.Buffer
+}
+
+func (b *syncBuffer) Write(p []byte) (int, error) {
+	b.mu.Lock()
+	defer b.mu.Unlock()
+	return b.buf.Write(p)
+}
+
+func (b *syncBuffer) String() string {
+	b.mu.Lock()
+	defer b.mu.Unlock()
+	return b.buf.String()
+}
+
+// captureDebugLogs redirects all zerolog output (global logger and context loggers) to a buffer
+// with debug logging enabled for all components. Everything is restored when the current spec ends.
+// Use it to assert that sensitive values never end up in log output.
+func captureDebugLogs() *syncBuffer {
+	buf := &syncBuffer{}
+
+	orgLogger := log.Logger
+	orgDefaultContextLogger := zerolog.DefaultContextLogger
+	DeferCleanup(func() {
+		log.Logger = orgLogger
+		zerolog.DefaultContextLogger = orgDefaultContextLogger
+		logging.SetStaticLoggingConfig(false, logging.Components{})
+	})
+
+	log.Logger = zerolog.New(buf).Level(zerolog.DebugLevel)
+	captured := log.Logger
+	zerolog.DefaultContextLogger = &captured
+	logging.SetStaticLoggingConfig(true, logging.Components{})
+	return buf
+}

benchmarks.task_description:
fix(ci): handle browser startup failures and provision media tests

Linux Test runs repeatedly failed at the first browser launch with only “the browser did not open its DevTools port”; earlier native video runs also failed without the media plug-ins and an audio output. Main run 43839844455 had 2274 passing tests and this one browser failure, while its Apple job passed.

Wait for browser readiness for up to 30 seconds, honor cancellation, report early process exits with the last 8 KiB of stderr, and reap the browser before removing its profile. The DevTools handshake now uses the startup context. Provision GTK’s GStreamer backend, audio/video plug-ins and a PulseAudio null sink so the Linux media test runs instead of skipping or failing for missing infrastructure.

Validation:
- `go tool nsgo check` passed.
- Browser startup exit/cancellation regressions and the real DevTools token/reload browser test passed (3 tests).
- Both new regressions fail against the original implementation.
- `actionlint` passed.
- Complete tool package suite: 164 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped.
- Hosted Linux suite: 2283 passed, 0 failed, 25 skipped; the real browser token/reload test and native media playback test both ran and passed.
- Hosted Apple tests, all-target Check, CodeQL and repository quality checks passed.

+package main
+

+	}

+}
+
+func TestBrowserStartupHonorsCancellation(t *testing.T) {
+	fakeBrowser(t, "exec sleep 60\n")
+	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 300*time.Millisecond)
+	defer cancel()
+	start := time.Now()
+	_, err := startBrowser(ctx)
+	if !errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded) {
+		t.Fatalf("startup error = %v, want the context deadline", err)
+	}
+	if elapsed := time.Since(start); elapsed > 3*time.Second {
+		t.Fatalf("canceled browser took %s to stop", elapsed)
+	}
+	checkBrowserProfileRemoved(t)
+}

+func fakeBrowser(t *testing.T, body string) {
+	t.Helper()
+	if runtime.GOOS == "windows" {

## Problem

When an Agent is offline during a shared-entry TLS verification cycle, the resulting failure can remain visible after the Agent reconnects and the entry recovers.

## Change

On an authenticated Agent startup or return from an offline heartbeat interval, schedule the existing bounded verifier for that Agent's shared entry when its latest error is the exact SNI/TLS check failure. Recovery operations remain fenced; the normal revision, DNS, TLS, service and application checks still determine readiness. Normal heartbeats do not continuously retry failed entries.

Related to https://github.com/petauron/vastora/issues/1363

Name a rehearsal role added only after it renders

Follow-up to #6115. It fixes the findings from that PR's review, which arrived after the merge.

- A role was recorded among the added objects before the render that writes it ran. A failed render then produced an `AddedError` naming a role the baseline never wrote. The role is now recorded once its pass renders.
- The filter that took an added role out of `RolesOutOfScope` is removed. Nothing that renders or compares the baseline reads that list, and no test could tell the filter was there.
- New tests pin a second pass of the loop, where a role created in the first pass is granted another role, and a render that fails. Moving the bookkeeping before the render fails the second test. Stopping after one pass fails the new row of the first.
- The docs say the role is created with the target's attributes and no password.

No engine-level test is added. This changes only what an error reports and drops a no-op, and #6115's e2e test covers the statements the dev server receives.
